subject: Coffee & Tea
title: CO₂ and Degassing
description: Learn CO₂ and Degassing in one minute.

hook.text: Freshly roasted coffee releases CO₂ for days. That gas is both friend and enemy of great coffee.

buildup.text: Roasting produces CO₂ trapped inside the bean's cellular structure. It escapes slowly after roasting.

discovery.text: Too much CO₂ repels water during brewing, causing uneven extraction. That's why fresh beans need rest.

twist.text: Most specialty roasters recommend waiting 3–7 days after roasting before brewing for optimal flavor.

climax.text: After about three weeks, most CO₂ is gone. Staling begins as oxygen takes over. The clock is ticking.

punchline.text: Too fresh is chaotic. Too old is flat. The sweet spot is brief.

quiz.question: Why should you wait a few days before brewing freshly roasted coffee?
options: Excess CO₂ repels water and causes uneven extraction
